The *Seriṇīpetivatthu* (Pv 31), rendered in English as "The Ghost Seriṇī", is a verse narrative belonging to the *Petavatthu* collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. The narrative addresses the karmic retribution that unfolds when greed clouds a person's moral judgment [SuttaCentral]. The text has been translated into five modern languages according to the SuttaCentral catalog [SuttaCentral].

No secondary literature passages were identified for this text in the corpus. However, substantial Pali-internal text reuse is documented: the *Petavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* contains 118 shared segments covering the verses of the text (§§1.1–9.6) [DharmaNexus]. The text also shares significant stock passages and verse units with several other *Petavatthu* narratives, including *Gaṇapetavatthu* (Pv 45), *Nandāpetivatthu* (Pv 16), *Mattāpetivatthu* (Pv 15), *Saṁsāramocakapetivatthu* (Pv 13), and *Sāṇavāsītherapetavatthu* (Pv 27) [DharmaNexus]. In automated cross-language searches, DharmaNexus aligns individual segments with the Sanskrit *Āryasaṃghāṭasūtra* and the Tibetan *Vinayavastu* (*Dul ba gzhi*, D0001), though SuttaCentral lists no confirmed historical parallels in other canonical languages [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
